attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript written by Kimi K3.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-hlww17rl/call-1e6edc5f3d7d423bb98d3dcee6376c9c/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la && ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
import shutil
for tool in ['python3','pdftotext','pdftoppm','pdfinfo','gs']:
 print(tool,shutil.which(tool))
for mod in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
 print(mod,importlib.util.find_spec(mod))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES', len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 text = p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(text)
 print(f'\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n{text}')
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for p in folder.iterdir():
 if p.name.startswith('page-') and p.suffix in {'.png', '.txt'}:
  p.unlink()
folder.rmdir()
print('Temporary PDF inspection files removed.')
PY"

strengths: MaskSub offers a simple, technically coherent way to incorporate heavy masking into supervised training. Its shared-weight, stop-gradient formulation adds no inference cost or model parameters, while token removal reduces the auxiliary training cost for ViTs.

The central ImageNet results are convincing across model sizes and training lengths. Table 1 reports gains of 0.6–0.7 percentage points at 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 points at 800 epochs. Three-seed results substantiate key improvements: ViT-B increases from 83.46±0.04 to 84.08±0.02 in Table A.13.

The paper meaningfully accounts for additional computation. Table 8 shows ViT-B reaching 84.1% in 25 GPU-days versus 83.7% for longer baseline training in 26 GPU-days. Table 9 also reports better accuracy and lower training cost than CoSub under the tested recipe.

Evaluation extends well beyond one classification configuration, covering ResNet, Swin, pretrained-model finetuning, downstream recognition, segmentation, detection, and robustness. For example, ViT-B gains 0.6 single-scale mIoU on ADE20K, and its ImageNet-A accuracy improves from 36.8% to 41.9%. This breadth supports practical usefulness.

The appendix substantially strengthens the submission through mask-ratio, loss-weight, and branch-count ablations, additional compute comparisons, and repeated experiments. Clear pseudocode, detailed vision training recipes, and a supplied code link support reproducibility.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is narrower than the framing suggests. With detached teacher predictions, Equation (3) has the same optimization gradient as KL-based consistency regularization. Thus, the stated distinction between MaskSub's distillation loss and UDA's consistency loss does not establish a new objective. The contribution chiefly concerns the effective integration and validation of masking within supervised recipes.

The explanation of automatic difficulty control exceeds the demonstrated evidence. Figure 2 shows aggregate optimization and gradient trends, but the distillation gradient depends on disagreement between predictions, not directly on teacher correctness. This does not establish the claim that masked learning is applied exclusively to successfully predicted examples. Table A.6 also leaves unclear whether 'without KD' removes auxiliary supervision or replaces it with hard-label supervision, limiting interpretation of that control.

The broadly positive applicability claims need qualification. Adding MaskSub during finetuning reduces ViT-B CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.89% to 89.55% in Table A.10. Section 4.2 explicitly states that CLIP's best-checkpoint accuracy is unchanged, so its reported improvement concerns final-epoch performance. Hierarchical architectures also require approximately twice the training computation, making the practical tradeoff architecture dependent.

Uncertainty reporting is uneven. Although repeated experiments support the central DeiT results, several smaller improvements—such as BEiTv2's 0.1-point finetuning gain and COCO's 0.2 box-AP gain—lack corresponding variability estimates. These extensions provide weaker evidence than the main classification experiments, without overturning the overall case for acceptance.
